off.title: The device list is off
off.body: Turn on the Inventory module to view, declare and add devices. Existing data is kept.

chip.fragileHint: Passive listening only, never actively scanned, so it does not hang.
chip.privateMacHint: Its MAC is a private (randomised) address the device picks for itself and changes, so it may show up again under a new one.
chip.quietHint: Private address, not added yet. It is not in To review: it has no open service and has not stayed long. It moves to To review if it opens a service or keeps coming back for more than a day.
chip.declaredHint: A product you said you run, with no address or name. Nothing scans it; it is checked against exploited vulnerabilities by its product.

declared.title: Declared software, no device
declared.body: You said you run this product (from Add, a CSV file or the weekly question) without naming a device or an address. Vedette checks it against exploited vulnerabilities by its product and never scans it. To tie it to a machine, add the software on that device instead and remove this entry.

sources.title: Sources
sources.info: What tells Vedette about this device. Several can feed it at once: an agent's values come first, then SNMP, then scans, then passive listening. Values you enter win over all of them.
sources.boxChecked: The box read its packages and open ports again.

what.scan: The box's active scan, in the scan window you set: open ports, services and a guess of the operating system.
what.snmp: Read-only questions to the device, with the community or v3 user set up on it here: maker, model and firmware version, as the device states them. For switches, routers, printers and firewalls.
what.agent: osquery on the machine (or Wazuh) sends its installed software with exact versions. For PCs and servers; on network gear SNMP reads the firmware version. When the machine gets a new address, its reports stay on this device.

state.offByHand: Off · Added by hand: nothing is sent to it until you turn this on

waiting.agent: Waiting for the agent to enroll

boxRow.scan: Not scanned: the box lists its own open ports
boxRow.snmp: Not needed: the box reads itself

state.ignored: Not read: the device is ignored

scan.firstTonight: On · first check tonight at {{time}}, in the scan window
scan.firstToday: On · first check today at {{time}}, in the scan window
scan.firstTomorrow: On · first check tomorrow at {{time}}, in the scan window
scan.firstDay: On · first check on {{day}} at {{time}}, in the scan window
scan.firstNow: On · first check runs during this scan window
scan.firstNext: On · first check in the next scan window
scan.checked: On · last check {{when}}: nothing answered yet

waiting.off: On · first check waits: active discovery is off
waiting.scope: On · first check waits: the scan ranges are not confirmed
waiting.outside: On · first check waits: the device is outside the scan ranges

scan.on: On: scanned in the scan window, inside the scan scope, with every safety rule. Turning it off stops all scan traffic to it, a scan running on it included.
scan.off: Off: no scan packet goes to this device. What scans found stays; values you entered still win.

snmp.on: On: read with the SNMP settings of this device at its read address; outside the LAN ranges only because it is on here; never if excluded. Turning it off stops all SNMP to it.
snmp.off: Off: no SNMP read goes to this device. What it read stays; values you entered still win.

agent.on: On: the agent's data of this device counts. Turning it off refuses its data and its readings stop counting.
agent.off: Off: the agent's data of this device is refused and its readings do not count. Turning it on takes them again.

scan.on: Network scan on for {{name}}: it is scanned in the next scan window if it is inside the scan scope.
scan.off: Network scan off for {{name}}: nothing more is sent to it.

snmp.off: SNMP off for {{name}}: nothing more is sent to it.

agent.on: Agent data on for {{name}}: the agent is asked to send its software now.
agent.off: Agent data off for {{name}}: its readings no longer count.

list.meta: Open a device for each value's source and confidence.
list.metaInfo: New values are added; old values are never overwritten.
list.titleBoxOnly: Only the Vedette box so far

col.name: Name
col.neverSeenTitle: Never seen on the network. Added by hand on {{when}}.
col.neverSeenAdded: Never seen on the network, added by hand {{when}}

table.caption: Device list
table.emptyApproved: No devices added yet. New devices wait under To review.

empty.title: No devices yet
empty.body: Plug the box into your LAN; Vedette finds devices within about an hour.
empty.info: You can also add devices manually or import a list from a CSV file (for example from Excel).
empty.bodyNeutral: Devices appear as the sensor hears them, usually within an hour.
empty.bodyBoxOnlyNeutral: Other devices appear as the sensor hears them.
empty.bodyWatching: Vedette is watching your saved ranges; devices appear within about an hour.
empty.bodyBoxOnlyWatching: Vedette is watching your saved ranges; other devices appear as it hears them.
empty.bodyBoxOnly: Add devices manually, or set your network ranges so Vedette finds them.

pending.description: New devices wait here until you add them to your devices.
pending.approveAllBody_one: This adds the 1 device listed here to your devices. A device marked unknown stays in the list.
pending.approveAllBody_other: This adds the {{count}} devices listed here to your devices (the list as it is filtered now). Devices marked unknown stay in the list.
pending.approveAllFailed: Added {{done}} of {{count}} devices, then it stopped: {{error}}
pending.descriptionInfo: A device seen on the network for the first time stays here until you add it. If it needs no watching, such as a staff phone, ignore it. If you do not recognise it, remove it from the list. Removing does not disconnect it.
pending.notifyOn: You will be notified about new devices.
pending.notifyVia: Notifications go through the channels you set up.
pending.notifyOff2: The Notifications module is off, so alerts cannot be sent yet.
pending.ignoredLater: Find it later under Devices → Ignored.

delete.title: Remove {{name}} from the list?
delete.body: This removes it from Vedette's list only, not the real device.
delete.comesBack: If the device is still on your network, it comes back under To review. To keep it out, choose Ignore instead.
delete.bodyInfo: Vedette sees it again the next time it talks on the network. Ignore keeps a device in the list as known and not watched, and it stays out of To review.
delete.findings_one: This device has {{count}} finding; removing the device removes it too.
delete.findings_other: This device has {{count}} findings; removing the device removes them too.
delete.findingsInfo: If the device shows up again it is assessed from scratch.

add.title: Add a device
add.body: Choose how Vedette learns about the device.
add.bodyInfo: Vedette alerts you when an actively exploited vulnerability matches it, even if the box is not plugged into your network yet.
add.versionHint: With the version, alerts are more precise. Leave empty if unknown.
add.name: Host name
add.nameHint: The name it has on your network, for example "fw-hq".
add.ipHint: IPv4, or a host name below. One of the two is needed.
add.done: Added {{name}}. Vedette will alert you when an actively exploited vulnerability matches this product.
add.softwareBody: Pick software running on this device to get alerts that match it.
add.doneKev_one: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerability in this product; Vedette will alert you when it matters.
add.doneKev_other: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerabilities in this product; Vedette will alert you when it matters.
add.softwareDoneKev_one: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerability in this software.
add.softwareDoneKev_other: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerabilities in this software.
add.needAddress: Enter an IP address or a host name, so Vedette knows which device this is.
add.ipBad: That IP address is not valid. Enter something like 192.168.10.25.

picker.placeholder: Type a product, model or maker, for example FortiGate 60F
picker.hint: Type a product, maker or model, for example fortigate 60f or synology.
picker.none: No matching product. Try the maker (Fortinet, Synology) or another name, or enter it yourself below.
picker.kev_one: Exploited in real attacks before: {{count}} vulnerability
picker.kev_other: Exploited in real attacks before: {{count}} vulnerabilities
picker.notListed: Can't find it? Enter the maker and product yourself
picker.customNote: Alerts still match by maker, even without an exact product.
picker.customNoteInfo: Vedette matches alerts by maker, so you still hear about exploited vulnerabilities in this maker's products even without an exact product match.
picker.more_one: {{count}} more match. Keep typing to narrow the list.
picker.more_other: {{count}} more matches. Keep typing to narrow the list.

import.title: Import devices from CSV
import.body: Import a list of devices from a CSV file, for example from Excel.
import.bodyInfo: The first row must be column titles: name, ip, product, version, kind. At least name or product is needed. Wrong rows are reported by line number; correct rows are still added.
import.tooLarge: The file is larger than {{kb}} KB. Split it into smaller files and import them one by one.
import.working: Importing the file… this can take up to a minute.
import.notesHint: These rows were added. Check them:
import.errorsHint: Fix these rows in your file, then import only them, to avoid duplicates.

detectedNotice.label: Detected {{field}}
detectedNotice.kept: Keeping your value. This notice shows again if the detected value changes.

detail.title: {{name}}: {{kind}}, last seen {{when}}
detail.meta: Every observation is kept for comparison. For each field Vedette uses the value you entered; otherwise it ranks the sources: agent first, then SNMP, then what the device announces about itself over LLDP, then the network scan (its operating system is a guess from the device's answers), then passive listening. Within the same source the higher confidence wins, then the newest observation.
detail.renameHint: Shown on every page. Leave it empty for the default name, {{name}}. The host name seen on the network does not change.
detail.renameBad: A name cannot contain < or >, control characters or invisible characters.
detail.fragileOnHint: Scanned gently once, then only listened to.
detail.fragileInfo: Vedette scans a fragile device gently once when it first sees it, then only listens (unless regular scans are allowed below).
detail.fragileOffHint: Vedette may scan this device during the scan window.
detail.origin: How it got on the list
detail.regularScanHint: After the first gentle scan, Vedette only listens to a fragile device or one of unknown type unless regular scans are allowed. Never means never, for every type of device.
detail.firstScanNone: No gentle first scan (added manually, the Vedette box itself, or a known type that is not fragile)
detail.metaLineNeverSeen: {{kind}}, added by hand {{when}}, never seen on the network

approval.pending: This device is not added yet
approval.body: Add it to your devices if you recognise it.
approval.bodyInfo: Until then it is still tracked but stays in the waiting list.
approval.quiet: This device uses a private address and is not added yet
approval.quietBody: Phones and laptops change their private address, so this one is not in To review while it shows nothing to look at. It moves there if it opens a service or keeps coming back for more than a day. Add it to your devices if you recognise it.

privateMac.note: This device uses a private (randomised) MAC address.
privateMac.noteInfo: Phones and laptops pick one per network and may change it, so the address can differ the next time and a device seen again under a new address is joined to this one by its host name when that name is its own.

obs.title: All observations
obs.description: Every value recorded for this device, with its source and confidence.
obs.descriptionInfo: Each time a sensor, a scan or you record a value, it is added here.
obs.caption: Observations for this device
obs.notUsedType: Not used: nmap's guess does not fit the device type

services.title: Open services
services.description: Open ports found by scans of this device, or listed by its agent or by the box itself.
services.descriptionInfo: A normal scan replaces this list with the ports it found open: nmap's 1000 most common ports and the usual alternate admin ports (SSH on 22222, HTTPS on 10443 and the like). Once a week a device that is not fragile gets a scan of every port, in the scan window.
services.descriptionInfo2: A gentle scan only adds ports, and a scan that timed out changes nothing. An agent (osquery, Wazuh) and the box itself list the ports they listen on, each as its own row. A port not seen for 90 days is removed.
services.caption: Services open on the device
services.name: Service
services.emptyBody: The active sensor has not scanned this device yet.
services.emptyBodyInfo: Check the scan window in Settings, Scanning, Safety, or press Check this device now under Last checks on the Overview tab to identify it at once.
services.emptyFragile: Fragile device: scanned gently once, then only listened to.
services.emptyFragileInfo: Set Regular scans on the Overview tab to allow them if you want it checked again.
services.emptyBox: The box lists the ports it listens on itself, every hour; none has come yet.
services.emptyBoxInfo: vedette-host reads them from the box's own socket tables (no scan): a port on every address or on one of the box's network cards. A port only the box itself reaches (loopback, a container bridge) is not listed.
services.emptyBoxContainer: A container-only install does not list the box's own ports.
services.emptyBoxContainerInfo: The box reads its open ports through vedette-host, which a container-only install does not have. Scan the machine from another box, or install an agent on it, to see them.
services.emptyAgent: Its agent lists the ports this machine listens on; none has come yet.
services.emptyAgentInfo: osquery reports them within minutes of enrolling, then every hour; Wazuh at each pull, from its syscollector ports scan. A port only this machine can reach (loopback) is not listed.

software.title: Software
software.description: The more exact the version, the more accurate the alerts.
software.descriptionInfo: Open findings lists the exploited vulnerabilities Vedette matched to this software's version and that are still open.
software.caption: Software on the device
software.name: Software
software.guessNoVersion: No exact version: a scan guess
software.correctionUndone: Undid your correction of {{name}}. Vedette uses what the sources read again.
software.newerWins: If a newer version is detected later, Vedette uses it automatically.
software.askedAgent: Asked the agent to send its software list now.
software.emptyBody: Use "Add software" to say what runs on this device.
software.emptyBodyInfo: Or install an agent so Vedette reads it by itself.
software.editBody: Findings follow the version you enter.
software.editBodyInfo: Vedette matches exploited vulnerabilities by version. Leave it empty if you do not know.
software.edited: {{name}} is now version {{version}}. Findings are matched again.
software.editedNone: Removed the version of {{name}}. Findings are matched again.
software.notInstalledBody: Vedette stops matching it and closes the findings only it produced, as long as the scan or agent reads this same version.
software.notInstalledBodyInfo: If a later read finds it at another version, that is a new install and Vedette checks it again. Clear undoes this.
software.notInstalledStale: You said not installed on {{date}}; the last read now finds {{now}} ({{source}}), and Vedette checks that.
software.notInstalledGone: You said not installed on {{date}}; no scan or agent reports it now.
software.cleared: {{name}} is back as the scan or agent reads it. Its findings are checked again.
software.pkgVersionHint: As the device's package manager shows it, for example 10.2_p1-r1. Empty removes it.
software.editedPkg: {{name}} is now package release {{release}}. Findings are matched again.
software.editedPkgNone: The package release of {{name}} is removed. Findings are matched again.

notes.title: Notes
notes.label: Notes about the device
notes.placeholder: For example: in the accounting room, maintained by ABC company.

setup.title: Sensor and agents
setup.meta: How Vedette hears your network: its sensor, and the agents on your devices.
setup.forbidden: You do not have access to this page
setup.forbiddenBody: The {{role}} role is needed to change the sensor and agent tokens. Ask an administrator for access or to do it for you.

network.title: LAN ranges
network.description: Internal network ranges Vedette may actively scan.
network.descriptionInfo: The passive sensor still hears everything it can see.
network.rangeHint: CIDR with prefix length, for example 192.168.10.0/24.
network.rangeHintInfo: Internal addresses only: 10.x, 172.16 to 172.31, 192.168.x, 100.64 to 100.127. Other prefix lengths work too, for example 192.168.10.0/25.
network.noRanges: No ranges yet. Add at least one range to let Vedette scan.

problem.empty: Type a range first. Write it like 192.168.10.0/24.
problem.noPrefix: "{{value}}" has no prefix length. Add it so Vedette scans the right size of network, for example {{value}}/24 or {{value}}/25.
problem.format: "{{value}}" is not a valid range. Write it like 192.168.10.0/24.
problem.hostBits: {{value}} is not written correctly: the address part must be the first address of the range. Use {{net}}.
problem.notPrivate: {{value}} is not an internal range, so it cannot be added here. To scan public addresses, use External exposure after verifying ownership.
problem.overlap: {{value}} overlaps {{other}}, which is already in the list. Keep the larger range and remove the smaller one.

note.network: {{from}} was added as {{to}}, the first address of its range.

network.changedElsewhere: Someone else changed the scan scope since you opened this page, so nothing was saved. The current values are shown again: check them and save.
network.fixFirst_one: Fix or remove the {{count}} range marked in red to save.
network.fixFirst_other: Fix or remove the {{count}} ranges marked in red to save.

active.title: Active scanning
active.description: A light scan for open ports and versions, only in the ranges above.
active.descriptionInfo: Automatic scans run inside the time window below; the first pass after active scanning is turned on runs at once, and Check this device now on a device identifies the devices you pick at once.
active.off: Active scanning is off, so Vedette only listens passively. Turn on the Active sensor module to learn open ports and versions.
active.crossMidnight: If the end time is earlier than the start (for example 22:00 to 05:00) the window runs past midnight. Pick hours when few people use the network.
active.rateHint: Slower is safer for old devices.
active.exclusionsHint: For example production machines or medical devices.
active.exclusionsHintInfo: Devices or ranges never actively scanned. Enter an IP or range and press Add.
active.badExclusion: Enter one IP (192.168.10.10) or a valid range (192.168.10.0/28, where the address part is the first address of the range).
active.safety: Active scanning only probes ports and reads versions. No exploitation, no denial of service.

fragile.title: Device types scanned only once
fragile.description: These types are scanned gently once, then only listened to.
fragile.descriptionInfo: A device of unknown type is treated the same until it is classified. Every other type counts as the group it belongs to here: an IP phone, a UPS or a PLC as an IoT device, a laptop as a computer, a VPN gateway as a firewall.
fragile.note: Each device gets one scan at the lowest speed. To allow regular scans, switch it on for the type below. You can still change a single device on its detail page; changes here apply to devices you have not changed individually.

scope.title: Confirm the scope
scope.confirm: I confirm these network ranges belong to my company and I am allowed to scan them.
scope.notConfirmed: Not confirmed yet. Active scanning can only be saved after you confirm the ranges.
scope.asIs: Vedette is provided as is. Its authors are not responsible for how you use it, including scanning.
scope.rangesChanged: You added or changed ranges. Tick to confirm before saving.
scope.willConfirm: Will be recorded as confirmed by you when you save.

sensors.title: Sensor on this box
sensors.description: The sensor listens to the network to learn devices without scanning.
sensors.descriptionInfo: It hears DHCP, ARP, mDNS, SSDP and LLDP. The port it listens on and SPAN are set in Settings → Box network.
sensors.descriptionNoSpanInfo: It hears DHCP, ARP, mDNS, SSDP and LLDP. It listens on the box's management port, set in Settings → Box network.
sensors.descriptionContainerNoSpanInfo: It hears DHCP, ARP, mDNS, SSDP and LLDP. On this container-only install you choose the card it listens on here with Configure.
sensors.descriptionContainerInfo: It hears DHCP, ARP, mDNS, SSDP and LLDP. On this container-only install you choose the card it listens on, and the SPAN card, here with Configure.
sensors.off: The passive sensor is off, so Vedette does not discover new devices by itself. Devices you add manually still work.
sensors.caption: Sensors on this box
sensors.startHint: Start it with compose.sensors.yaml on this machine.
sensors.startingHint: The box is starting the sensor (after setup or after you turned it on). This can take a few minutes; the row updates by itself.
sensors.notStartedHint: The box could not get the sensor running.
sensors.notStartedHintInfo: Turn Passive sensor off and on in Settings → Modules to try again now; on the box, journalctl -u vedette-sensor and journalctl -u vedette-core say why.

capture.label: Capture
capture.no_permission: It cannot open the network card: capturing needs root and CAP_NET_RAW, which a rootless Docker or Podman does not give. Start the sensor as root.
capture.no_interface: The card it should listen on is not on that machine. Choose another card.
capture.filters_invalid: The capture filters cannot be read, so it captures nothing until they change.
capture.capture_failed: The capture keeps failing and is retried; the sensor's log says why.

card.body: Choose the card the sensor listens on.
card.bodyInfo: Pick among the cards it reported, and say whether it is a SPAN card that receives mirrored traffic. This machine's network is yours: Vedette does not change the card.
card.bodyNoSpanInfo: Pick among the cards it reported. This machine's network is yours: Vedette does not change the card.
card.spanKept: {{name}} is saved as a SPAN port. This version of Vedette no longer sets SPAN up: you can untick it, not tick it again.
card.label: Listen on
card.hint: Choose the card on the network you want to discover.
card.hintInfo: Run ip -br address on this machine to see which card has which address.
card.autoChosen: Automatic (the one card of this machine with an address)
card.span: SPAN port: this card receives the switch's mirrored traffic
card.spanHint: Prepare the card on this machine first: no IP address, promiscuous mode, connected to the switch's mirror port.
card.spanNeedsCard: Choose a card under Listen on first: SPAN is set on one named card, not on Automatic.
card.notListening: The sensor is not listening on any card. Choose one below.
card.notListeningInfo: By itself it only takes the one card of this machine that has an address, and there is not exactly one.
card.none: No card reported yet: start the sensor with compose.sensors.yaml.

sensors.configBody: The port the sensor listens on and whether mirrored traffic is arriving. Change them in Settings.
sensors.configBodyNoSpan: The port the sensor listens on: the box's management port, set in Settings.
sensors.spanLink: Configure SPAN in Settings → Box network
sensors.spanHint: Vedette reads DNS queries, TLS server names, HTTP hosts and connection metadata from the mirrored traffic to learn devices and spot connections to known-bad addresses. It does not store packet contents. Without mirrored traffic the sensor only sees broadcast messages (DHCP, ARP, mDNS).

quiet.since: Agent quiet since {{when}} — check the service on the device
quiet.sinceUnknown: Agent quiet — check the service on the device
quiet.whereWindows: On the Windows machine, in PowerShell as Administrator:
quiet.whereLinux: On the machine, in a shell with root rights:
quiet.sysv: Without systemd: sudo /etc/init.d/osqueryd status, then sudo /etc/init.d/osqueryd restart.
quiet.runningBody: Then it cannot reach Vedette at {{box}}. Check that this machine can open that address, that no firewall or proxy blocks it, and that the box address has not changed.
quiet.runningBodyNoBox: Then it cannot reach Vedette. Check that this machine can open the box address, that no firewall or proxy blocks it, and that the box address has not changed.
quiet.repair: If the box address changed or the agent keeps stopping, run the install command from Devices > Sensor and agents > Agents again: the current script points the agent at the box and makes the service restart itself after a failure.

neverReported.title: Agent running, but it has not reported anything yet
neverReported.body: It calls Vedette, so the service is running, but it has delivered no results since it was installed. If it stays like this, run the install command again from Devices > Sensor and agents > Agents on that machine, or check that its address is one Vedette knows.

machines.title: Machines with an agent
machines.body: Each agent is judged by its own schedule: it asks the box for its settings every 5 minutes, and is quiet after three missed calls.
machines.caption: Machines with an osquery agent
machines.removed: {{host}} was removed from the list. If its agent still runs, it enrols again by itself.
machines.replacedNote: A newer agent of this machine reports. Remove this old record.
machines.neverNote: It calls Vedette but has delivered nothing yet.

onDevice.title: Install osquery on {{name}}
onDevice.body: Run one command on this machine. It then reports its installed software with exact versions.

setup.title: Agent setup of {{name}}
setup.body: The token made for this device and the install command to run on it.
setup.lost: The token itself was shown once, when it was made: put it in place of <TOKEN>.

check.title: Agent on {{name}}
check.off: Off for this device: its data is refused.
check.calls: It reports every {{every}}; it is called quiet after three of those without a call.
check.pulls: Vedette pulls from the Wazuh server every {{every}}; quiet after three pulls without this device.
check.reachBody: On the machine, test that it can open Vedette at {{box}}: no firewall or proxy may block it.
check.reachBodyNoBox: On the machine, test that it can open the box address: no firewall or proxy may block it.
check.wazuhBody: This device is read through your Wazuh server.

agents.title: Agents on servers
agents.description: An agent tells Vedette exactly which software runs on a server.
agents.descriptionInfo: With an agent, alerts say "confirmed" instead of "suspected".
agents.recommendation: Use osquery on your Linux and Windows PCs and servers. Already run Wazuh? Connect its API instead.
agents.serverOnly: Vedette supports Linux and Windows, on PCs and servers. macOS is not supported yet.

boxAddress.change: Change it in Settings → Box network
boxAddress.container: It is the first name in VEDETTE_HOSTS.
boxAddress.otherHost: You opened Vedette at {{here}}, but agents will use {{box}}.

agents.off: Agent intake is off. Turn this module on to create osquery tokens and connect Wazuh.

osquery.introInfo: Each machine reports its operating system and installed packages (and Windows hotfixes). osquery changes nothing on the machine.

agents.caption: Enrollment tokens
agents.emptyBody: Use "Create agent token", then run the one command it shows on each server.

page.downloadBody: The official osquery {{version}} packages, served by this box.
page.downloadBodyInfo: The install command in a token downloads the right one by itself. Download a package here to copy it to a server yourself (a USB stick works) or to install it with your own tools.
page.checkHint: Before you install, check the file: sha256sum <file> on Linux or Get-FileHash <file> in PowerShell must print the SHA-256 in the table. The package alone reports nothing to Vedette: the agent also needs an enrollment token.
page.none: This box has no copy of the osquery packages.
page.noneInfo: There is nothing to download here, and the install command stops at the package download. Update Vedette to the release, which ships them.
page.tokenBody: The dialog shows the one command that installs and enrolls osquery.
page.tokenBodyInfo: It also shows the manual steps for a package you installed yourself.

agents.configBody: Replace <TOKEN> with the token you saved when you created it.
agents.configBodyInfo: If you lost it, revoke it and create a new one.
agents.sampleHint: Preview build only: there is no backend yet, so this pretends the machines reported in.
agents.sampled: Sample data received: {{devices}} devices updated, {{software}} software entries added from the agent.
agents.revokeBody: Agents using this token are rejected immediately. Data already received is kept.
agents.name: Token name
agents.nameHint: To remember which machines use it, for example "osquery on SRV-AD".
agents.expiryHint: After this the token stops working. You can revoke it earlier.
agents.createNoteInfo: This makes one enrollment token and shows the install command with it. The token is shown once. A token that no machine has used expires after 24 hours; once a machine has enrolled, it works for the lifetime you see in the list.

removeUnused.hint: Removes every token with no machine enrolled now. Tokens with machines stay, and so do tokens made in the last hour, in case their command is still on screen.

agents.createdBody: Pick the operating system and run the one command below on the server.
agents.tokenOnce: The token is shown once: copy it somewhere safe before you close this dialog.
agents.tokenOnceInfo: After you close this dialog Vedette keeps only the last 4 characters.

noAddress.title: Servers cannot reach this box at the address you opened it with
noAddress.body: Open Vedette at an address other machines can reach.
noAddress.container: You opened Vedette as localhost, and the box knows no other address, so no install command can work yet. Agents need an address of this machine that other machines can reach: in vedette.env put this machine's LAN address in VEDETTE_BIND_IP and that address (or a name that points to it) in VEDETTE_HOSTS, run docker compose --env-file vedette.env up -d again, and open Vedette at that address. The command appears here then.
noAddress.appliance: You opened Vedette as localhost, so this page does not know an address that other machines can reach and no install command can work yet. Open Vedette at the box's network address (Settings → Box network shows it); the command appears here then.
noAddress.token: The token stays valid: keep it, and use it with the command once it appears.

platform.label: Operating system
platform.detected: Operating system: {{os}}, as this device reports it.
platform.pick: Choose the operating system of the machine to get its install command.

install.title: Install with one command
install.linuxHow: Run as root, or with sudo, on the machine.
install.linuxHowInfo: Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux; x86_64 or arm64.
install.windowsHow: Run in PowerShell as Administrator on the machine.
install.windowsHowInfo: Windows 10 or 11, or Windows Server 2019 or later; Windows PowerShell 5.1 or later. Not yet proven on a real Windows Server: its first run found a certificate problem, fixed since and to be run again.
install.worksOn: Works on Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL family, SUSE, Amazon Linux, Alpine and Arch. Run as root or with sudo.
install.otherDistros: Other distributions: use the command above.
install.shaHint: The box uses its own certificate, so the command first downloads the script without trusting it, then refuses to run unless the script's SHA-256 matches the value above. The script carries the box certificate and checks every later download against it. The servers need no Internet: the box serves the osquery package too, after checking its checksum.
install.windowsWhy: Windows PowerShell 5.1 cannot skip certificate checks for a single request, so the command uses curl.exe -k for that one download only, and checks the hash before anything runs.
install.readFirstBody: Read it before you run it. Running it again upgrades or repairs the installation.
install.uninstall: Remove osquery from the server again
install.security: The token only enrolls osquery and reads nothing from Vedette.
install.securityInfo: It is shown once, expires (7 days by default) and can be revoked. It is sent as an argument and in a header, never in a web address. Every install and enrollment is recorded in the audit log.
install.advancedBody: The same result step by step, for locked-down servers or your own packaging.
install.advancedBodyInfo: The package comes from this box and is installed only when its SHA-256 matches the table above. For a file you copied over (USB stick), leave out the download line: on Linux run the first and last lines in the folder that holds the file; on Windows set $f to the file's path, then run the last line.
install.queriesBody: Read-only queries, delivered through the config endpoint.
install.queriesBodyInfo: Packages differ per distribution, so each machine runs only the ones that fit it. The interfaces query reports the machine's IPv4 addresses and MAC addresses so Vedette can match it to the right device. In its first hour after enrolling, a machine runs every minute each query whose answer Vedette has not received yet, so its operating system and packages show within a few minutes; it then follows the intervals below.
install.queriesBodyInfo2: Vedette adds the machine to your devices, because whoever made the token vouched for it, and sets its type from its operating system (Windows Server and Linux: Server; other Windows and macOS: PC) unless a person has chosen one.

download.title: Or download the package
download.body: For a server without network access, or to install it your own way.
download.bodyInfo: Download the official osquery package from this box, copy it to the server (a USB stick works), check its SHA-256 and install it. Then follow the enrollment steps under Download and install manually.
download.caption: osquery packages this box serves
download.none: This box has no copy of the osquery packages for this operating system.
download.noneInfo: So the command below stops at the package download. Update Vedette to the release, which ships them.

linux.installDeb: Download osquery from the box, check it and install it (Debian, Ubuntu)
linux.installRpm: Download osquery from the box, check it and install it (RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux)
linux.secret: Save the token and the box certificate, then check the fingerprint

windows.install: Download osquery from the box, check it and install it
windows.secret: Save the token and the box certificate, then check it
windows.service: Install and start the osqueryd service

agents.fingerprint: The downloads in the manual steps use -k, because the box certificate is not trusted yet: the package is installed only when its SHA-256 matches the value on this page, and the certificate step prints its fingerprint for you to compare with the one from your Vedette administrator. osquery verifies the certificate on every later request.
agents.ownPaths: The /api/v1/install/… and /api/v1/intake/… paths are Vedette's own. Everything else follows the osquery and Wazuh documentation.

wazuh.title: Wazuh
wazuh.intro: Vedette reads agents and packages from the Wazuh server API.
wazuh.introInfo: It reads the agent list, operating systems, installed packages and Windows hotfixes. Nothing is installed on your agent machines, and the Wazuh user can only read.
wazuh.disconnectBody: Vedette stops syncing and deletes the stored password. Data already received stays.

status.never: Connected, waiting for the first sync

wazuh.formBody: Enter a read-only Wazuh API user; the steps below create one.
wazuh.formBodyInfo: Nothing is installed on your agent machines.
wazuh.stepsTitle: 1. Create a read-only API user on the Wazuh manager
wazuh.stepsBody: Run these on a machine that can reach the Wazuh API.
wazuh.stepsBodyInfo: The user may only read the agent list and the syscollector inventory (agent:read and syscollector:read).

steps.login: Log in to the Wazuh API
steps.link: Attach the policy to the role and the role to the user

wazuh.urlHint: The Wazuh manager, port 55000 by default, for example https://wazuh-manager:55000.
wazuh.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
wazuh.passwordHint: Stored encrypted. After saving only the last 4 characters are shown.
wazuh.limit: At least 5 minutes. The Wazuh server answers slowly to frequent pulls.
wazuh.testOk: Connected to Wazuh {{version}}. This user can see {{count}} agents.
wazuh.waiting: Reaching the Wazuh manager… this can take up to 30 seconds.

box.title: This is the Vedette box itself
box.lead: It is always the first device.
box.packagesAppliance: Its packages are read from the box (dpkg) every hour and right after an OS update, so the version list is exact. No osquery agent is needed on the box.
box.packagesContainer: The package list of this machine is not available in a container-only install.
box.matched: It is matched against exploited vulnerabilities like any other device.
box.noFix: No update fixes these yet: see each finding.
box.noDelete: The box cannot be removed from the list: Vedette runs on it.

incidents.info: What Vedette raised about this device that is not handled yet: a trap it touched, an intrusion attempt against it, a connection to a known-bad address. Open one to acknowledge or resolve it.

guess.title: Most likely: {{kind}} ({{category}})
guess.hint: Vedette's guess from what it has seen. Until you confirm it, scans still treat this device as unknown and careful.
guess.alternativesInfo: Pick the right one: the type decides whether Vedette scans the device gently as fragile.

addDialog.body: Pick how Vedette learns about the device.
addDialog.bodyInfo: Use several at once on the same device: an agent's values win over SNMP, SNMP over a scan, a scan over passive listening. Devices on your LAN are also found by themselves and wait under To review.

title.snmp: Add a device and read it with SNMP

info.manual: Name the device by its IP address or host name and pick the product it runs, in three clicks. Vedette alerts you when an actively exploited vulnerability matches it. A device you add yourself is never scanned.
info.snmp: Vedette reads a device's maker, model and firmware with read-only SNMP questions in every scan window. Enter its address and its community or v3 user here; the device is added with SNMP on. You can change them later on the device's own page.
info.osquery: Create a token, then run one command on the server. osquery reports installed software with exact versions, so alerts say confirmed instead of suspected.
info.wazuh: Vedette reads the agents and packages of your Wazuh server through its read-only API. Nothing is installed on the machines.
info.csv: Columns name, ip, product, version and kind; up to 500 rows. Wrong rows are reported by line, correct rows are still added.

snmp.addressHint: The address the device answers SNMP on. Vedette reads only this address.
snmp.productHint: Pick its product, for example a FortiGate. SNMP then fills in the exact model and firmware.
snmp.needProduct: Pick the product the device is.
snmp.submit: Add device and turn SNMP on
snmp.addedNotSet: {{name}} was added, but its SNMP settings were not saved
snmp.addedNotSetBody: Fix the settings below and save again; the device is not added twice.

osquery.noMac: macOS is not supported: osquery runs on Linux and Windows servers.
osquery.noMacInfo: Vedette reads servers. Laptops and Macs are seen by the network scan and passive listening.

addDialog.moduleOff: Module is off: turn it on here

needs.snmp: SNMP reads run in the Active sensor module, which is off.
needs.osquery: osquery reports arrive through the Agent intake module, which is off.
needs.wazuh: Wazuh is read through the Agent intake module, which is off.

search.label: Search devices
search.placeholder: Name, IP, MAC, maker, or type:switch

key.has: Has findings, software or open ports
key.risk: Risk: exploited findings or an update recommended

possible.same: As another device (merge or keep separate)

declaredPage.title: Declared software
declaredPage.description: Products you run that are not tied to a device.
declaredPage.info: For example Microsoft Office, a cloud service or a branch firewall you cannot reach. They come from your answers to the weekly question, a CSV row with only a product, or Add here.
declaredPage.info2: Vedette matches each one against exploited vulnerabilities by its product, so they feed Findings like a device. Nothing scans them. To tie one to a machine, add the software on that device's page and remove it here.
declaredPage.addBody: Pick a product you run to get alerts when it is exploited.
declaredPage.addInfo: Use this for software with no device in the list. For software on a known device, open the device and add it there.
declaredPage.done: Added {{name}}. Vedette will alert you when an actively exploited vulnerability matches it.
declaredPage.doneKev_one: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerability in this product; Vedette will alert you when it matters.
declaredPage.doneKev_other: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerabilities in this product; Vedette will alert you when it matters.
declaredPage.caption: Declared software
declaredPage.emptyBody: Add a product you run that is not on a device in the list.
declaredPage.emptyInfo: Your answers to the weekly question ("I have this") appear here too.
declaredPage.elsewhere_one: {{count}} product declared without a device is in
declaredPage.elsewhere_other: {{count}} products declared without a device are in

inline.modulesPage: Turn it on in Settings, Modules (admin)
inline.alsoOn: Turning it on also turns on {{list}}, which it needs.

snmpNext.scopeWhy: An administrator adds it to the scan scope.
snmpNext.scanningWhy: Active scanning is off, so the box sends nothing to devices.
snmpNext.scanning: Turn on active scanning in Scope
snmpNext.neverWhy: This device is set to Never scan.
snmpNext.never: Change it on the device page
snmpNext.notListedWhy: Vedette has not found this address yet. The next scan or the sensor finds it; add it under To review, then read it here.
snmpNext.publicWhy: {{ip}} is a public address: Vedette only reads devices inside your own network.
snmpNext.turnSnmpOn: Turn SNMP on for {{ip}} and read it
snmpNext.snmpOn: SNMP is on for {{ip}}. Reading it now.
snmpNext.excludedSnmpWhy: {{ip}} is on the exclusion list, which Vedette never touches, not even with SNMP. The LAN ranges only govern discovery and network scans.

toScope.title: Add {{range}} to the scan scope
toScope.body: Vedette only scans and asks SNMP inside the ranges you allow.
toScope.info: Vedette sends scans and SNMP questions only inside these ranges, and only after someone confirms they belong to the company.
toScope.restWhy: The scan window, speed and fragile types stay as they are.
toScope.changed: Someone changed the scan scope meanwhile. Check the ranges above and tick again.

merge.bulkTooMany: Select {{max}} devices at most: one device and {{from}} that join it.
merge.bulkBoxLeftOut: The Vedette box is left out: it is always its own device.
merge.title: Merge {{count}} devices
merge.description: One device stays; the others join it and leave the lists. Split an address off to undo.
merge.info: Use this when several rows are one machine: the interfaces of a firewall or router, a server with two network cards, a phone with a new private Wi-Fi address. The device you keep keeps its id, main address, notes, settings and findings history; the addresses, software, open ports and findings of the others move to it, and it is found by any of its addresses. It is added to your devices when one of them was. Split off an address on its Addresses list to make it a device of its own again.
merge.keepHint: Picked for you: the one with an agent, the one you added, a name or the most findings.
merge.differHint: Pick the name, type and operating system the device keeps. The maker, model and host name follow the sources.

move.nothing: Only the records of the other devices: they have no address, software, open port or finding.

merge.previewFailed: Vedette could not read what this merge would do.
merge.loading: Reading what the merge would do…
merge.doneHint: Split an address off on its Addresses list to undo.

pick.title: Merge {{name}} with…
pick.description: Select the rows that are this same machine.
pick.search: Search by name, IP or MAC
pick.empty: There is no other device to merge with.
pick.max: {{count}} devices at most join one device in one step.
pick.loadFailed: The device list could not be read.

reason.same_name_cards: Same name on two network cards
reason.mac_at_added_device: Seen at a device added by hand

addresses.title: Addresses
addresses.info: Every network address the device was seen at: the device is found by any of them. The main address is the one lists show and scans and reads go to. Split off an address that belongs to another machine: that interface, its IP and MAC together, becomes a device of its own with what was read only there.
addresses.noneBody: Nothing has seen this device on the network yet.
addresses.blockAgent: The agent reports from this address: it stays with the agent's machine.
addresses.blockOnly: The only address of this device.
addresses.splitBody: That interface, its IP and MAC together, becomes a device of its own with what was read only there.
addresses.splitStays: What an agent or SNMP read of the whole machine stays with {{name}}, and Vedette will not offer the two as the same device again.
addresses.splitMain: This is the main address: {{next}} becomes the main address of {{name}}.
addresses.splitDone: {{address}} is now a device of its own.

same.title: Possibly the same device as
same.titleMany_one: Possibly the same device as {{count}} other device
same.titleMany_other: Possibly the same device as one of {{count}} other devices
same.info: Vedette could not be sure these rows are one machine: phones and laptops change their private Wi-Fi address, and many share a name such as "iPhone". Merge keeps one device with its approval, notes and findings, and moves the other one's addresses, software and findings to it. Keep separate means Vedette will not ask again for these two. Two machines that agents or hardware MAC addresses tell apart are never offered.
same.keptSeparate: Kept separate from {{name}}. Vedette will not ask again for these two.
same.keepBody: Vedette will not ask again for these two and will not join them on its own. This cannot be undone.
same.hintMany_one: Possibly the same device as {{name}} or {{count}} other
same.hintMany_other: Possibly the same device as {{name}} or {{count}} others

watch.staysIgnored: {{into}} stays ignored: it is not scanned and the open findings that move from {{from}} close.
watch.staysWatched: {{into}} stays watched: the findings of {{from}} that closed when it was ignored reopen.
watch.watchedAgain: {{into}} is watched again, because {{from}} is a device you added and watch: its findings that closed when it was ignored reopen.

risk.findingsAria: open its findings with this status
risk.inputAria: Vedette needs your answer about this device: open its questions
risk.info: Red: the device has open findings, CVEs that are being exploited. Amber: none of those, but a recommended update fixes a CVE likely to be exploited (EPSS 10% or more) or of high or critical severity (CVSS 7 or more). No mark: neither.
risk.unavailable: Risk marks could not be read just now, so none are shown and the risk filter is not applied. Findings still lists what to fix.
risk.unavailableOne: Risk mark not available right now.

ignore.title: Ignore {{name}}?
ignore.body: Use this for a device that needs no watching, such as a staff phone. Vedette keeps it in its list, so it is the same device when it is seen again, but stops watching it:
ignore.review: It leaves To review and sends no new-device alert.
ignore.scans: Vedette stops scanning it and reading it over SNMP.
ignore.findings: Its open findings are closed as not relevant, with the reason "device ignored", and it is no longer checked for exploited vulnerabilities. Findings you already settled keep their status.
ignore.noFindings: It is no longer checked for exploited vulnerabilities.
ignore.still: when it touches a trap or the intrusion detection reports it: a staff phone probing your network is exactly what you need to hear about.
ignore.privateMac: It uses a private Wi-Fi address ({{mac}}). Phones change this address from time to time; when this one does, it comes back in To review as a new device, and you can ignore it again.
ignore.undo: You can stop ignoring it at any time under Devices → Ignored or on its page: it comes back to To review and the findings Ignore closed reopen.

ignored.title: This device is ignored
ignored.body: Ignored {{when}}. Vedette does not scan it, read it over SNMP, alert about it as a new device or check it for exploited vulnerabilities; its open findings were closed. A trap hit or an intrusion alert from it still reaches you.
ignored.description: Devices you said need no watching, such as staff phones.
ignored.descriptionInfo: They are not scanned and raise no new-device or vulnerability alerts; a trap hit or an intrusion alert from one still reaches you.

deviceSnmp.title: SNMP
deviceSnmp.description: Read-only SNMP questions to this device: maker, model, serial number and firmware, as it states them.
deviceSnmp.descriptionInfo: Vedette sends only read-only GET requests, in the scan window and when you press Check now, to one address: the device's IP, or the management address you set as Read from. The community or passwords are stored encrypted and shown only by their last 4 characters.
deviceSnmp.notSetUpBody: Set up SNMP to read this device's maker, model, serial number and firmware. Switches, routers, firewalls, printers and UPS usually answer.
deviceSnmp.noIp: This device has no address yet: SNMP can be set up once a sensor has seen its address.

why.working: The last read at {{ip}} got an answer.
why.waiting: Set up, not read yet: the next scan window reads it, or press Check now.
why.notAnswering: The last read at {{ip}} got no answer.

deviceSnmp.notReady: SNMP reads are not available right now

check.pending: Reading {{ip}} with SNMP… this takes up to 15 seconds.
check.pendingNoIp: Reading the device with SNMP… this takes up to 15 seconds.

deviceSnmp.secretShort: Saved (too short to show its end)

answer.title: What answered at {{ip}}
answer.check: If this is not the device you expect, Read from points at another device: edit it.

title.moved: Moved: the device's IP changed; set the read address again
title.secret_lost: The saved community or password was not restored
title.other: Nothing is sent to this device now

deviceSnmp.removeBody: Vedette deletes this device's SNMP settings and its community or passwords. What the device already said stays in the inventory, and its SNMP switch under Sources stays as it is.
deviceSnmp.savedOn: SNMP is now on for this device.

form.body: Read-only: Vedette only sends GET requests, never SET.
form.bodyInfo: The community or passwords are stored encrypted on the box and sent only to the Read from address; afterwards only their last 4 characters are shown. SNMPv1, MD5 and DES are not offered: they are not secure.
form.readFromHint: Leave empty to read the device's IP, {{ip}}.
form.readFromHintNoIp: Leave empty to read the IP you enter above.
form.readFromInfo: Use a management address when the device answers SNMP only on another interface, for example a firewall whose SNMP listens on its management port. What answers there is recorded on this device. Any address on your local networks, not the Vedette box.
form.copyNone: Copies the version, user, community or passwords and port of a device that already has SNMP set up.
form.copyHintNoIp: The box copies the saved community or passwords itself; they never reach this browser. They are sent only to this device's own IP.
form.copyHint: The box copies the saved community or passwords itself; they never reach this browser. They are sent only to this device's own IP, {{ip}}.
form.copyOwnIpOnlyNoIp: A copied community or password goes only to this device's own IP. To read it at {{target}}, choose "Don't copy" and type them.
form.copyOwnIpOnly: A copied community or password goes only to this device's own IP, {{ip}}. To read it at {{target}}, choose "Don't copy" and type them.
form.copyWhat: Copies {{name}}'s SNMP settings: {{version}}, UDP port {{port}}, with its saved community or passwords.
form.v2cClear: v2c sends the community in clear text on your network. Use v3 when the device supports it.
form.communityHint: The read-only community the device accepts.
form.keep: Saved: ends in {{last4}}. Leave empty to keep it.
form.keepShort: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
form.again: Read from changed: type it again, so it is sent to the new address only because you said so.
form.portHint: Only if the device answers SNMP on another port. Leave empty for 161.
form.consentOff: Saving turns SNMP on for this device (Sources): Vedette then sends read-only SNMP questions to {{ip}} in the scan window and when you press Check now.
form.consentOffNoIp: Saving turns SNMP on for this device (Sources): once you enter its IP, Vedette sends read-only SNMP questions to it in the scan window and when you press Check now.
form.consentOnNoIp: Vedette sends read-only SNMP questions to the device's IP in the scan window and when you press Check now.
form.consentOn: Vedette sends read-only SNMP questions to {{ip}} in the scan window and when you press Check now.

error.readFromBad: Enter an IPv4 address, like 192.168.1.1, or leave it empty for the device's IP.
error.readFromNotLocal: {{ip}} is not a local network address ({{ranges}}): SNMP reads stay on your own networks.
error.secretAgain: Read from changed: type it again to send it to the new address.
error.community: The community is 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters (no accents or emoji).
error.user: Use letters, digits and . _ @ - only, up to 64 characters.
error.passwordRequired: Enter the password, 8 characters or more.
error.password: Use printable ASCII characters only (no accents or emoji), up to 64.
error.port: Enter a port from 1 to 65535, or leave it empty for 161.
error.readFromReserved: {{ip}} is a multicast, broadcast or reserved address, not the address of one device.

notices.title_one: Vedette changed an SNMP setting by itself
notices.title_other: Vedette changed {{count}} SNMP settings by itself

list.title_one: SNMP is set up on {{count}} device. Open one to edit it or check it now.
list.title_other: SNMP is set up on {{count}} devices. Open one to edit it or check it now.
list.label: Devices with SNMP set up
